scope: The post-trial and post-judgment course of a US federal civil money judgment, and the financing instruments whose terms it triggers, as they bear on the lender's collections: a bankruptcy petition (11 U.S.C. §362) and the borrower's cash above operating need on each due date. Templates are by forum and instrument; each case's dispute, components and financing instruments fill them. Any appeal is decided after the analysis period.
design: Each quantity has one source: the law, the record, measured data, arithmetic, a bounded term with a sensitivity, or Jev. Dates, amounts, cash, enforceability and legal meaning come from the first five. Jev answers one actor's decision at a time, given the path's dates, amounts and cash and the record items. Readings of the record are evidence for those decisions.

roles.agent: Groups the accepted findings about one obligation and gives its order reference (a docket reference, checked), its nature (from `natures`), the counterparty, the amount figure (checked against the quotes) and any judgment date (checked against the quotes).
roles.jev: Answers reading questions about the record, and forecast questions: one actor's decision at a time.
roles.host: Hydrates evidence, asks the questions, applies the stage rules, composes probabilities, simulates cash.

probability_label: Model judgment: Jev's probabilities for each decision, combined along each path.

natures.fee_and_cost_award: an award of attorneys' fees and costs

frcp_62a.citation: Fed. R. Civ. P. 62(a): "execution on a judgment and proceedings to enforce it are stayed for 30 days after its entry, unless the court orders otherwise."

frcp_62b.citation: Fed. R. Civ. P. 62(b): a party may obtain a stay by providing a bond or other security; "The stay takes effect when the court approves the bond or other security".

ebay_2006.citation: eBay Inc. v. MercExchange, L.L.C., 547 U.S. 388 (2006): a permanent injunction issues where the plaintiff shows irreparable injury, inadequate remedies at law, a balance of hardships in its favour, and that the public interest would not be disserved.

usc18_1836_b3a.citation: 18 U.S.C. §1836(b)(3)(A) (DTSA): in a civil action for trade-secret misappropriation a court "may" grant an injunction to prevent any actual or threatened misappropriation, on such terms as the court deems reasonable.

nc_66_154_a.citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. §66-154(a): actual or threatened misappropriation of a trade secret "shall be permanently enjoined upon judgment finding misappropriation" for the period the trade secret exists plus any further period the court deems necessary.
nc_66_154_a.modality: shall, on a judgment finding misappropriation

frcp_62c.citation: Fed. R. Civ. P. 62(c)(1): unless the court orders otherwise, an interlocutory or final judgment in an action for an injunction is not stayed after being entered, even if an appeal is taken.
frcp_62c.modality: shall, unless the court orders otherwise

frap_4a1a.citation: Fed. R. App. P. 4(a)(1)(A): notice of appeal within 30 days after entry of the judgment or order.

frap_4a4a.citation: Fed. R. App. P. 4(a)(4)(A): a timely motion under Rule 50(b), 52(b), 59 (alter or amend; new trial), or Rule 54 fees only where the court extends time under Rule 58(e), makes the time to appeal run from the order disposing of the last such remaining motion.

frcp_69a.citation: Fed. R. Civ. P. 69(a)(1): a money judgment is enforced by a writ of execution; the procedure must accord with the procedure of the state where the court is located.

usc28_1963.citation: 28 U.S.C. §1963: a judgment may be registered in another district "when the judgment has become final by appeal or expiration of the time for appeal or when ordered by the court that entered the judgment for good cause shown." Good cause: thin forum assets and substantial assets elsewhere (Associated Bus. Tel. Sys. v. Greater Capital Corp., 128 F.R.D. 63, 66-68 (D.N.J. 1989)).
usc28_1963.modality: may, after finality or on good cause

usc28_1961.citation: 28 U.S.C. §1961(a)-(b): interest from the date of entry of the judgment at the weekly average 1-year constant maturity Treasury yield for the calendar week preceding the judgment, computed daily, compounded annually. Increases by an amended judgment run from the amended date; a remitted amount keeps the original date (Kaiser Aluminum v. Bonjorno, 494 U.S. 827 (1990); Dunn v. HOVIC, 13 F.3d 58, 60-62 (3d Cir. 1993)); fees run from the judgment quantifying them (Eaves v. County of Cape May, 239 F.3d 527 (3d Cir. 2001)).
usc28_1961.rate_source: FRED WGS1YR (H.15 weekly), week ending 17 May 2024: 5.14%

nc_24_1.citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. §24-1: "The legal rate of interest shall be eight percent (8%) per annum".

nc_24_5_b.citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. §24-5(b): in an action other than contract, "any portion of a money judgment designated by the fact finder as compensatory damages bears interest from the date the action is commenced until the judgment is satisfied." The action commences with the original complaint, including for a claim added by amendment (Beach Mart, Inc. v. L&L Wings, Inc. (E.D.N.C. Mar. 26, 2021)).
nc_24_5_b.modality: shall, on the portion designated compensatory

nc_66_154_d.citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. §66-154(d): if willful and malicious misappropriation exists, "the court may award reasonable attorneys' fees to the prevailing party."

usc18_1836_b3d.citation: 18 U.S.C. §1836(b)(3)(D): if the trade secret was willfully and maliciously misappropriated, the court may award reasonable attorney's fees to the prevailing party. §1836(b)(3)(C): exemplary damages up to 2 times the damages awarded.

nc_75_16.citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. §75-16: once a violation of §75-1.1 is found, "judgment shall be rendered ... for treble the amount fixed by the verdict." The plaintiff elects between the trebled and the punitive recovery and takes the larger (United Labs. v. Kuykendall, 335 N.C. 183 (1993)).
nc_75_16.modality: shall, once a §75-1.1 violation is found

nc_1d.citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. §§1D-15(a), 1D-25(b): punitive damages are capped at the greater of 3 times compensatory damages or $250,000, and rest on compensatory damages, so a new trial on compensatory damages carries the exemplary award with it (Carawan v. Tate, 304 N.C. 696 (1982); Gasoline Prods. Co. v. Champlin Ref. Co., 283 U.S. 494 (1931)).

remittitur.citation: Remittitur is to the maximum the evidence supports, and the plaintiff may refuse it and take a new trial (Hetzel v. Prince William County, 523 U.S. 208 (1998); Kazan v. Wolinski, 721 F.2d 911 (3d Cir. 1983)).

jmol_standard.citation: Fed. R. Civ. P. 50(b); JMOL only where the record lacks the minimum evidence to support the verdict (Lightning Lube v. Witco, 4 F.3d 1153, 1166 (3d Cir. 1993)).

bond_amount.citation: A supersedeas bond secures "the whole amount of the judgment remaining unsatisfied, costs on the appeal, interest, and damages for delay" (Southern Track & Pump, Inc. v. Terex Corp., C.A. No. 08-543-LPS (D. Del.), quoting Poplar Grove Planting & Ref. Co. v. Bache Halsey Stuart, 600 F.2d 1189, 1191 (5th Cir. 1979)). The court may accept reduced or alternative security for good cause (Dillon v. City of Chicago, 866 F.2d 902, 904-05 (7th Cir. 1988); Poplar Grove).
bond_amount.unit: bps of the judgment + interest + costs

usc11_362.citation: 11 U.S.C. §362(a): a bankruptcy petition operates as a stay of any act to collect a claim against the debtor that arose before the petition.

usc11_303b.citation: 11 U.S.C. §303(b)(1): where the debtor has 12 or more creditors, an involuntary petition is filed by three or more creditors holding noncontingent, undisputed claims above the statutory threshold.

indenture_limitation_on_suits.citation: Indenture §7.06 (Limitation on Suits): "No Holder shall have any right to institute any proceeding, judicial or otherwise, in respect of this Indenture, or for the appointment of a receiver or trustee, or for any other remedy hereunder (other than in the case of an Event of Default specified in clause (j) or (k) of Section 7.01), unless: (a) the Holder of a Note gives to the Trustee written notice of a continuing Event of Default; (b) the Holders of at least 25% in Principal Amount of the then outstanding Notes make a written request to the Trustee to pursue the remedy; (c) such Holder of a Note or Holders of Notes offer and, if requested, provide to the Trustee indemnity reasonably satisfactory to the Trustee against any loss, liability or expense; (d) the Trustee does not comply with the request within 60 days after receipt of the request and the offer and, if requested, the provision of indemnity; and (e) during such 60-day period the Majority Holders do not give the Trustee a direction inconsistent with the request."

indenture_right_to_payment.citation: Indenture §7.07 (Unconditional Rights of Holders of Notes to Receive Payment): "Notwithstanding any other provision of this Indenture, the right of any Holder to receive payment of the Principal, the Redemption Price, or Interest, in respect of the Notes held by such Holder, on or after the respective due dates expressed in the Notes or any Redemption Date, as applicable, and to convert the Notes in accordance with ARTICLE 9, or to bring suit for the enforcement of any such payment on or after such respective dates or the right to convert, shall not be impaired or affected adversely without the consent of such Holder."

usc11_547.citation: 11 U.S.C. §547(b): transfers to a creditor within 90 days before the petition are avoidable; under §547(c)(4), new value the creditor gives after a transfer reduces the exposure.

indenture_final_judgment.citation: Indenture §7.01(i) (New York law, §17.10): an Event of Default occurs when "a final judgment or final judgments for the payment of money are entered by a court or courts of competent jurisdiction against the Company or any of its Subsidiaries and such judgment or judgments remain undischarged, unpaid or unstayed for a period (during which execution shall not be effectively stayed) of 60 days", above $10.0 million excluding amounts covered by insurance, after notice by the Trustee or the Holders of at least 25% in principal amount.
indenture_final_judgment.meaning: Whether a money judgment entered under Rule 58 while timely Rule 50(b) and 59 motions are pending is a "final judgment" under §7.01(i) is an open question; no New York decision addresses it. Under one reading the judgment entered on 20 May 2024 is a final judgment for the payment of money: the clause measures the default by whether the judgment is undischarged, unpaid or unstayed and whether execution is effectively stayed, and execution was available once the Rule 62(a) stay ended on 19 Jun 2024, so the 60 days end on 19 Aug 2024. Under the other reading a timely Rule 50(b) or 59 motion suspends the finality of the judgment until the order disposing of it (Banister v. Davis, 590 U.S. 504 (2020); Osterneck v. Ernst & Whinney, 489 U.S. 169, 174 (1989); both decide finality for an appeal), so the 60 days run from the order disposing of the last pending motion. The company's 424B5 of 23 May 2024 refers to a final judgment still to be rendered.

frcp_59a.citation: Fed. R. Civ. P. 59(a)(1)(A): after a jury trial the court may grant a new trial on all or some of the issues "for any reason for which a new trial has heretofore been granted in an action at law in federal court." A new trial may be granted even where the evidence is legally sufficient to support the verdict, when the verdict is contrary to the great weight of the evidence, so that a new trial is necessary to prevent a miscarriage of justice (Roebuck v. Drexel Univ., 852 F.2d 715, 735-36 (3d Cir. 1988)). "[N]ew trials because the verdict is against the weight of the evidence are proper only when the record shows that the jury's verdict resulted in a miscarriage of justice or where the verdict, on the record, cries out to be overturned or shocks our conscience" (Williamson v. Consolidated Rail Corp., 926 F.2d 1344, 1353 (3d Cir. 1991)). An award "so grossly excessive as to shock the judicial conscience" is set aside: the court remits it to the maximum recovery that does not shock the judicial conscience, or orders a new trial (Gumbs v. Pueblo Int'l, Inc., 823 F.2d 768, 771-74 (3d Cir. 1987)).

udtpa_trebling_authorities.citation: Trebling a trade-secret award after the jury answered 'No' to the unfair-trade-practices question: the authorities each side relies on. Against trebling: this court's order of 14 May 2024 on the defendants' Rule 50(a) motion (D.I. 590) held that North Carolina courts have "not recognized head start benefits to the Defendants as such a proxy" for the plaintiff's injury and that "[t]he jury has no reasonable basis to find compensable damages under the UDTPA, but has sufficient basis to find injury"; §75-16 trebles damages, and a restitutionary award is not trebled (Winant v. Bostic, 5 F.3d 767, 775-76 (4th Cir. 1993)); a violation of the Trade Secrets Protection Act is not in itself a violation of §75-1.1 (Drouillard v. Keister Williams Newspaper Servs., 108 N.C. App. 169 (1992); Legacy Data Access, LLC v. MediQuant, Inc. (W.D.N.C. 2017), which declined to treble a trade-secret verdict where the jury awarded $1 on the unfair-trade-practices claim); and Qorvo filed no Rule 50 motion, the route for setting aside a jury finding for want of evidence (Unitherm Food Sys., Inc. v. Swift-Eckrich, Inc., 546 U.S. 394 (2006)). For trebling: the jury finds the facts, and the court decides as a matter of law whether they amount to an unfair or deceptive practice (Hardy v. Toler, 288 N.C. 303 (1975)); "A violation of the Trade Secrets Protection Act constitutes an unfair act or practice under N.C. Gen. Stat. § 75-1.1" (Medical Staffing Network, Inc. v. Ridgway, 194 N.C. App. 649 (2009)); and Grout Doctor Global Franchise Corp. v. Groutman, Inc. (E.D.N.C. 2015), which Qorvo cites (D.I. 587).

events.entitlement_decided: the court has decided the payer is liable for this obligation
events.amount_fixed: the court has fixed this obligation's amount
events.judgment_entered: a money judgment for this obligation has been entered
events.appeal_filed: the payer has filed a notice of appeal against this obligation
events.stay_secured: the payer has stayed this obligation with a bond or other security
events.mediation_ordered: the court has ordered the parties to mediate or attend a settlement conference on this obligation
events.post_trial_motions_pending: timely post-judgment motions under Fed. R. Civ. P. 50(b), 52(b) or 59 that could change this obligation are pending and undecided
events.post_trial_decided: the court has decided every pending post-judgment motion that could change this obligation
events.injunction_entered: the court has entered an injunction in this dispute

readings.stage_rules_note: The stage is the most advanced procedural event any cited passage establishes, in the order listed. Pending post-trial motions place an entered judgment in post_trial: execution may issue once Rule 62(a)'s stay ends, the amount can still change, and the time to appeal runs from the last ruling (FRAP 4(a)(4)(A)). A ruling on every such motion moves it to judgment_entered. A dispute with no established event carries an evidence request.

amount_finality.label: How final the amount is
amount_finality.relevance: Does the quoted text say how far this obligation's amount has progressed (claimed, briefed or submitted for decision, fixed)?
levels: No amount has been stated
An amount is claimed or requested by a party
The amount has been fully briefed or submitted to the court for decision
The court has fixed the amount

appeal_intent.label: The payer's appeal intent
appeal_intent.relevance: Does the quoted text say whether the payer will appeal this obligation?
levels: The payer accepts the judgment or says it will not appeal
The passage states no position on an appeal
The payer is considering or reserves the right to appeal
The payer states it intends to appeal
appeal_intent.note: A filed notice of appeal is the procedural event appeal_filed.

appeal_barred.label: An appeal of this obligation is waived or barred
appeal_barred.relevance: Does the quoted text state that the payer waived, or is barred from, appealing this obligation itself?

debtor_resistance.label: The payer's willingness to pay this obligation
debtor_resistance.relevance: Does the quoted text describe the payer paying, refusing to pay, or resisting collection of an amount due under this obligation? Contesting the amount in court and appealing are litigation conduct, answered no.
levels: The payer paid amounts due under this obligation when they fell due
The passage describes no payment conduct by the payer on this obligation
The payer paid late, or only after a motion or an enforcement step by the payee
The payer has refused to pay an amount that is due, or has resisted its collection
debtor_resistance.note: One dimension: the timeliness of the payer's payment conduct relative to when payment fell due.

debtor_liquidity.label: The payer's ability to fund this obligation
debtor_liquidity.relevance: Does the quoted text say whether the payer can fund this obligation: its cash, its financing, or a statement about its ability to pay an amount of this size?
levels: The text indicates the payer cannot fund this obligation
The text indicates the payer could fund it only with strain (new financing, asset sales or cuts to operations)
The text indicates the payer can fund it without strain
debtor_liquidity.payer_note: Asked when the counterparty pays. The borrower's cash comes from its connected-bank data.

settlement_signals.label: Settlement signals
settlement_signals.relevance: Does the quoted text say anything about the parties' willingness or efforts to settle this obligation, including a refusal to settle or failed talks?
levels: A party refuses to settle, or settlement talks have failed
The passage describes no settlement discussion
A party expresses general willingness to settle
The parties disclose active settlement negotiations
The parties have an agreement in principle or a term sheet

outcomes.settled: The settlement is paid on its date: the company's available cash less its 30-day operating need, capped at the amount owed. The dispute ends.
outcomes.paid: Paid on the enforceable date: the amount owed plus statutory interest.
outcomes.vacated: The post-trial ruling leaves no money award.
outcomes.new_trial: A new trial is ordered on the component; the retrial falls after the analysis period.
outcomes.levied: An unstayed levy takes min(owed, reachable cash) on the levy date.
outcomes.stayed: Execution is stayed on approved security; collateral is locked on trajectories whose cash covers it.
outcomes.unresolved: The post-trial ruling falls after the analysis period on that trajectory; the judgment as entered stays enforceable.
outcomes.uncollected: Enforceable and unpaid at the end of the analysis period, with no levy.
outcomes.reorganization: A petition, voluntary or involuntary, on that trajectory's date; the lender's collections stop (§362).

dependence: A path is one sequence of decisions along the templates, each conditional on the earlier ones. Dates are drawn per trajectory, keyed (instance, node, purpose), independently of every probability; a decision takes effect on the trajectories where its condition holds on its date. Components combine by the chain rule into the ruling's outcomes. A decision's probability depends on the facts its question is given (the stage of the dispute, the amount owed, the stay and notes status); paths that share those facts share one answer.
constraints: A branch leaves a path when an event has occurred, a payment has ended the dispute, or arithmetic rules it out on every trajectory of the path. Every other branch stays, at whatever probability.

forum.supplied_by: agent (instantiate_dispute), code-checked against the quoted passages
forum.note: The templates cover the court forum; an arbitration dispute is instantiated once its award is confirmed, under the court stages.

fields.component_id: stable id within the dispute (e.g. unjust_enrichment, exemplary, patent, trebling, fees, prejudgment_interest)
fields.label: short label
fields.kind: compensatory | exemplary | patent | trebling | fees | prejudgment_interest | costs
fields.amount_cents: integer cents quoted in a cited passage (awarded or requested); null when statutory or unknown
fields.statutory: rule id in `rules` whose law gives the amount (e.g. nc_24_5_b)
fields.unknown: true when the record gives no amount and no rule computes one
fields.basis: the finding id and quote the amount or rule rests on
fields.motion: docket reference of the pending motion that decides it, if any

components_schema.checks: Every amount_cents appears in a cited quote; a statutory component names a rule in `rules`; a component is exactly one of amount_cents, statutory or unknown.

stages.arbitration_note: A confirmed award follows the court stages.

ruling_lag_days.basis: Days from the close of briefing to the ruling on this judge's fully briefed matters on this docket, entries on or before the review date (D. Del. 1:21-cv-1417; n = 10, median 61.5).
ruling_lag_days.draw: one lag per pending motion, drawn uniformly from the sample, independent across motions and of every probability; the motion is decided on briefing close + lag
ruling_lag_days.sensitivity: one common lag for every motion

briefing_days_new_motion.basis: D. Del. LR 7.1.2(b): answering brief 14 days after the opening brief, reply 7 days after the answer; a motion filed on day t closes briefing on t + 21 and is decided on that date + a ruling_lag_days draw.

levy_lag_days.basis: Days from the enforcement decision (with the judgment registered where cash sits) to the levy.

petition_lag_days.basis: Days from a decision to file to the petition.

holder_notice_lag_days.basis: Days from a ripe default to the holders' notice and acceleration.

holder_petition_route.basis: Indenture §7.06: no Holder may institute any proceeding in respect of the Indenture unless it has given the Trustee written notice of a continuing Event of Default, Holders of at least 25% have made a written request to the Trustee to pursue the remedy and offered indemnity, the Trustee has not complied within 60 days, and the Majority Holders have given no inconsistent direction in that period. §7.07: each Holder's right to receive payment of principal and interest on or after its due date, and to sue for it, is unimpaired. Base: §7.06 governs the holders' involuntary petition, so it comes no earlier than their request, made at acceleration, plus 60 days. Sensitivity: the holders may file at once on acceleration. The default, the notice and acceleration, and the petition are separate dated events.

stay_restart_on_increase_days.basis: Rule 62(a) stays the increase from an amended judgment for 30 days from its entry (base); sensitivity: the whole amended amount waits 30 days.

bond_forward_interest_years.basis: The bond covers the judgment, accrued §1961 interest and interest over the appeal; costs: none filed as of the review date.

bond_collateral_share_bps.basis: Surety practice for a borrower below investment grade: full cash collateral; lower bound 80%.

stay_security.basis: Rule 62(b): a stay takes effect when the court approves the bond or other security. Where the company's cash at approval covers the bond collateral, the collateral is locked on approval. Otherwise the company proposes reduced security: its available cash above its 30-day operating need on the day it moves; if the court approves, that amount is locked on approval. Base: where that amount is zero, the stay is not effective. Sensitivity (noncash): such a stay rests on security or a waiver not in cash, and nothing is locked.

reachable_before_registration.basis: Cash a levy reaches before the judgment is registered where the cash sits: none (base); all consolidated cash (sensitivity).

levy_scope.basis: A levy after registration reaches the company's consolidated cash, including cash it needs to operate.

settlement_date_in_interval.basis: A settlement agreed in a stage of the dispute is paid 30 days after the stage begins (base) or at its end (sensitivity).

cash_floor.basis: The cash floor is the first date available cash falls below the 30-day operating need of the collection rule (base) or below zero (sensitivity). Where the company keeps operating at the floor, it decides again on the first date its available cash falls below zero.

form25_after_panel_days.basis: The stock is not listed from its suspension (base); sensitivity: Form 25 effectiveness at the panel decision + 60 days (Rule 5820 windows) + 10 (17 C.F.R. §240.12d2-2(d)(1)), or suspension + 10 without a hearing.

suspension_after_determination_days.basis: Nasdaq Rule 5815(a): a timely hearing request stays suspension; without one, suspension follows the Staff Determination after the 7-day request window.

panel_decision_days.basis: Days from the Staff Determination to the Hearings Panel's decision.

repurchase_date.basis: Fundamental Change repurchase: notice within 20 business days, repurchase 20-35 business days after notice (indenture §10.01). Base: latest date; sensitivity: earliest.

coupon_cash_share.basis: The notes' interest, $44.0M at 6.0% a year payable semi-annually on 15 June and 15 December (8-K of 9 Jun 2022), is $1.32M on 15 Dec 2024, paid on the next business day. Indenture §16.02(c): interest is paid in shares unless the company elects cash; the shares delivered equal the payment divided by 95% of the ten-trading-day average VWAP. §9.02(k): without stockholder approval the shares delivered in respect of the notes may not exceed 11,403,332, and the company pays cash in lieu of shares above that limit. The company can issue 3.0 million authorized, unissued and unreserved shares (424B5, 23 May 2024). Base: shares up to that capacity at 95% of the 24 May 2024 registered direct price of $0.20, about $570,000, and the remainder, about $750,000, in cash. Sensitivities: the whole coupon in cash; the whole coupon in shares, which the capacity covers at a price of $0.4632 or more. A reverse split changes the price and the share quantities by its ratio, so the amount the capacity covers is unchanged; the record before the review date gives no ratio, so pre-split quantities apply on every path. No coupon is paid after a bankruptcy petition.

chips_credit_cents.basis: 13 May 2024 call: refundable CHIPS ITC of $2.8M-$4.0M "over the next 9 to 12 months", undated; paid through the FY2024 return (26 U.S.C. §48D(d)). Base $0 within the analysis period; sensitivity $2.33M prorated June-December (within the sourced $1.38M-$2.63M).

legal_fee_spend.basis: Legal spend in the feed continues until the dispute resolves on the path (payment, settlement, vacatur, petition), then stops.

judgment_default_reading.basis: Which judgment starts the 60 days in indenture §7.01(i) is an open question of New York contract law (rule indenture_final_judgment). Base: both readings. The default can ripen 60 days after the Rule 62(a) stay of the judgment as entered ends (19 Aug 2024), where the judgment is unpaid and execution is not effectively stayed; where the holders do not act then, it can ripen again 60 days after the order disposing of the last pending tolling motion, on the amount that survives the ruling. Sensitivities: the judgment as entered only; the post-trial ruling only.

remittitur_scenarios.note: Declared scenarios, each run on its own. On the remit branch with the creditor accepting, the compensatory component takes the selected scenario's amount; under verdict_stands that branch is priced at the verdict.

remitted.label: Remitted to $23.1M, the most the evidence supports
remitted.basis: Bennis's method with Irwin's revenue corrections: 54% off $50.3M, or 65% off $66.1M (D.I. 616-1, tr. 1698-1700, 2346-47)

fee_scenarios.note: The requested amount if the court awards fees; $0 if it denies them.

settlement_scenarios.note: The settlement amount is the company's available cash on the settlement date less its 30-day operating need, floored at zero and capped at the amount owed; a settlement exists only where that amount is positive. Declared scenarios, each run on its own. A settlement books cash. A paid settlement ends the dispute and with it the judgment default.

scenarios.lump_sum: the settlement amount, paid on the settlement date; the claim is released on payment
scenarios.monthly: the settlement amount in equal monthly payments from the settlement date to the end of the analysis period; no payment after a bankruptcy petition; the claim is released when the last payment is made

settlement_scenarios.asked: once in each stage: before the post-trial ruling; from the ruling to the appeal deadline; while the judgment is enforceable and unstayed; while it is stayed

excluded_branches.branch: appeal decided within the analysis period
excluded_branches.basis: A notice of appeal follows the last post-trial ruling (FRAP 4(a)(4)(A)); Federal Circuit schedules put any decision after the analysis period.
Neither was sought as of the review date.
Leaves a path when the collateral exceeds available cash on every trajectory of the path at the stay decision; the stay then rests on the court's approval of lesser security.
Leaves a path when the amount owed exceeds available cash on every trajectory of the path at the decision date.

excluded_branches.branch: pay the accelerated notes or the repurchase
excluded_branches.basis: Leaves a path when the principal exceeds available cash on every trajectory of the path.
The line is below the $2.5M cross-default threshold; the first interest default date falls after the analysis period.
The record before the review date gives no revenue by part; the injunction runs as one stress scenario.

excluded: the $8.0M customer note of 26 Jun 2024, after the decision date

federal_post_judgment.instrument: money judgment in US district court

intervals.I1: from the review date to the post-trial ruling (the last order changing the judgment)
intervals.I2: from the post-trial ruling to the appeal deadline
intervals.I3: judgment enforceable and unstayed, from the later of the date it is enforceable and the appeal deadline

record_items: the public grounds of the motion for a new trial or remittitur of the trade-secret damages
the trial evidence on the amount of trade-secret damages that the motion cites

the pending motions and their grounds

indenture_convertible.instrument: convertible notes under a New York-law indenture

terms_from_instrument.judgment_default: Event of Default (§7.01(i)): final money judgments above the threshold, excluding amounts covered by insurance, remain undischarged, unpaid or unstayed for the stated period, during which execution is not effectively stayed; it takes effect on notice by the trustee or holders of 25% of principal.
terms_from_instrument.listing_default: Event of Default (§7.01(b)): the common stock is not listed on an Eligible Market; it takes effect without notice or grace period.
terms_from_instrument.acceleration: Acceleration (§7.02): on an Event of Default the trustee or holders of 25% may declare the notes due; a bankruptcy petition makes them due automatically; holders of a majority may rescind once every default is cured, and a judgment default is cured by payment, discharge or a stay.
terms_from_instrument.repurchase: Fundamental Change repurchase (§10.01): delisting lets each holder require repurchase at 100% of principal plus accrued interest in cash; notice within 20 business days, repurchase 20-35 business days after notice; failure to repurchase is an Event of Default.
terms_from_instrument.interest: Interest (§16.02): paid on each interest date, in shares unless the company elects cash.

clocks.judgment_default_ripe: per judgment_default_reading: the end of the Rule 62(a) stay of the judgment as entered + the instrument's period; and, where the holders did not act then, the order disposing of the last pending tolling motion + the instrument's period; each with the judgment unpaid and not effectively stayed; then the holders' notice and acceleration + holder_notice_lag_days; the issuer's petition at acceleration, the holders' per holder_petition_route
clocks.listing: board vote call 20 days before the split must take effect; split effective by the first of the 10 consecutive business days ending on the compliance deadline; Staff Determination the day after the deadline; hearing request within 7 days; suspension + suspension_after_determination_days without a hearing; panel decision + panel_decision_days with one; 'not listed' per form25_after_panel_days. The chain runs where no acceleration of the notes precedes the vote call; delisting is a default only where the notes are not already due

order: I1: settlement, execution, stay, debtor response, early registration
ruling (chain rule over the merits decisions)
I2-I4: settlement, appeal, stay, debtor response, enforcement, judgment default
composition.ruling_chain_rule: P(outcome) = product of the merits answers along its branch, in order: liability, damages, remittitur election, patent, then trebling, fees and interest where trade-secret money survives. Outcomes group into amount classes by arithmetic: none; each distinct amount within reach of available cash on some trajectory; and amounts beyond available cash on every trajectory, grouped where their dates and cash are identical (increased and not-increased amounts in separate groups).

composites.notes_petition: the holders accelerate, then the issuer files, or else three holders file (petition_on_notes + (1 - petition_on_notes) x holders_involuntary); the notes are then either the subject of a petition, due and unpaid with no petition, or not accelerated
composites.listing: board x approval, else hearing x exception

composition.neutral: Attribution step 2 sets every residual to neutral (a Noul at 0.5, a Choice uniform over the branches arithmetic leaves) and keeps everything the record fixes.
composition.paths_to_the_engine: Paths are sequences of decisions; each decision's effect is dated per trajectory and applies only where its condition holds on that date. A petition ends every later effect on its trajectory.
composition.situation: Each question is asked in the conditions its node's situation names, each with its basis, that hold at the decision on every trajectory of the path where it is asked. A condition that holds on only some of them is left unstated.
